# Scripps reports Q3 2026 financial results


Nov. 5, 2026


By Carolyn Micheli


**CINCINNATI –** The E.W. Scripps Company (NASDAQ: SSP) delivered $545 million in revenue for the third quarter of 2026. Income attributable to the shareholders of Scripps was $20.7 million or 21 cents per share.


**Recent company events** :


- Through Election Day on Tuesday, Scripps generated $284 million in full-year Local Media division political advertising revenue – 44% above the 2022 midterm election cycle.


- Scripps continues to make progress on its company transformation plan and expense reductions to generate $125-$150 million of enterprise EBITDA growth by 2028 through cost savings and revenue initiatives. The impact of the transformation work will be most evident beginning in the fourth-quarter results as the company will have implemented about $100 million in annual run-rate savings by year end. In 2026, we reduced our workforce by about 20%.
- On the revenue growth side of the transformation, more than 70 initiatives are in the pipeline, focused on yielding more revenue from businesses we own and creating new revenue from adjacent business areas.
- By the end of the year, Scripps will have nearly completed its connected local newsrooms transformation, positioning its news operations for the streaming world to meet consumers where they are watching. The connected newsrooms integrate AI and automation technology to adapt stories for all digital and broadcast platforms, putting the news teams’ work in front of new audiences and driving new streams of revenue with a more durable cost structure.
- The Scripps Networks division’s third-quarter revenue benefited from Nielsen’s Sept. 1 ratings methodology change to more accurately measure over-the-air households after negative impact from their changes earlier in the year. Connected TV revenue grew 37%, and Scripps now expects it to end the year at about $155 million. Despite those tailwinds, pressure from the economy and the impact of low consumer confidence on direct response advertising led to revenue down 11% on an adjusted combined basis.
- Scripps Networks division adjusted combined expenses were up 0.9%, driven by the new WNBA contract this year. For the fourth quarter, the company expects division expenses to begin a downward trend as transformation cost initiatives take effect.
- The company ended the third quarter with $83 million in cash and will use that and cash from Q4 political advertising revenue to pay down at least $150 million of debt in the fourth quarter.


**From Scripps President and CEO Adam Symson** :
“During this contentious 2026 midterm election cycle, broadcast television continued to prove itself to be the best vehicle for reaching voters because we provide a trustworthy platform in a politically polarizing climate. Local TV platforms took nearly half of the record $11.9 billion spent this year, according to AdImpact. Scripps’ strong political footprint drove our full-year political ad revenue 44% above our 2022 midterm results. Our performance benefited from our local sports strategy, strong connected TV business and dedicated political sales force.


“The companywide transformation we launched in February is well underway and on track to deliver both on our commitment to evolve the company’s products and the expected benefit to enterprise EBITDA next year. Our goal is to ensure Scripps remains a strong media company positioned to serve our communities and preserve local journalism by adapting to how Americans consume news and information. In part aided by technology, our teams are producing more reporting from the field, deepening our community news coverage and expanding our reach to audiences across broadcast, streaming, digital and social platforms while improving the segment profit of our business.


“In our Scripps Networks division, we saw a modest sequential recovery in our third-quarter revenue and profit margin, bolstered by the early impact of Nielsen’s updated ratings methodology and 37% growth in revenue from our connected TV/streaming platform distribution. Disciplined expense management drove a year-over-year decline in total adjusted combined expenses when you factor out the first-year impact of our new WNBA contract.


“The work underway reflects our priorities to improve our earnings trajectory, strengthen the balance sheet and best serve American media consumers. At the same time, we continue to evaluate accretive M&A opportunities with discipline, focusing on transactions that enhance our financial position and strategic flexibility within our current balance sheet.”


**Operating results** Third-quarter company revenue was $545 million, an increase of 3.6% or $19 million from the prior-year quarter. Political revenue was $82.6 million, compared to $5.5 million in the prior-year quarter, a non-election year. Costs and expenses for segments, shared services and corporate were $427 million, down from $449 million in the year-ago quarter, reflecting tight expense controls and savings achieved through our enterprise-wide transformation plan.


Income attributable to the shareholders of Scripps was $20.7 million or 21 cents per share. The current-year quarter included $18.8 million in restructuring costs, which decreased the income attributable to shareholders by 14 cents per share. In the prior-year quarter, loss attributable to shareholders of Scripps was $49 million or 55 cents per share. The prior-year quarter included a $7.6 million loss on extinguishment of debt, $6.5 million of financing transaction costs, a $1.4 million write-off of deferred financing costs and $2.7 million in restructuring costs. When taken together, these items increased the loss attributable to shareholders by 15 cents per share.


***Third-quarter 2026 segment results compared to prior-period amounts:***


**Local Media** Revenue was $373 million, up 15% from the prior-year quarter.


- Core advertising revenue decreased 16% to $111 million, reflecting displacement from political advertising.
- Political revenue was $80.6 million, compared to $5.1 million in the prior-year quarter, a non-election year.
- Distribution revenue decreased $7.8 million or 4.2% to $178 million. Distribution revenues in the third quarter of 2025 included $10.7 million of revenue from WRTV and WFTX that were sold in the first quarter of 2026. Additionally, a service blackout during the contract negotiations with DirecTV had a $3.8 million third-quarter 2026 impact.


Segment expenses decreased 6.4% to $255 million.


Segment profit was $118 million, up from $52.8 million a year-ago quarter.


**Scripps Networks** Revenue was $173 million, down 14% from the prior-year quarter. Segment expenses were $140 million, down 5.2% from the prior-year quarter.


Segment profit was $33 million, compared to $53.3 million in the year-ago quarter.


***Third-quarter 2026 segment results compared to prior-period adjusted combined amounts:***


*In order to provide more meaningful year-over-year comparisons, we are providing non-GAAP supplemental information for certain revenues and expenses for the prior-year periods on an adjusted combined basis.*


*The adjusted combined revenue and expense information illustrates what the historical results of Scripps would*


*have been, given the assumptions outlined in the supplemental materials and had WFTX, WRTV and WTVQ (Local*


*Media) and Court TV (Scripps Networks) transactions been effective at the beginning of 2025. Refer to the*


*“Supplemental Information” section that begins on page E-8 of the attached tables.*


**Local Media – Adjusted combined basis** Revenue was $373 million, up 19% from the prior-year quarter.


- Core advertising revenue decreased 13% to $111 million, reflecting displacement from political advertising.
- Political revenue was $80.6 million, compared to $5.3 million in the prior-year quarter, a non-election year.
- Distribution revenue was $178 million, flat from the prior-year quarter.


Segment expenses decreased 3.1% to $255 million.


Segment profit was $118 million, compared to $49.8 million in the year-ago quarter.


**Scripps Networks – Adjusted combined basis** Revenue was $173 million, down 11% from the prior-year quarter. Segment expenses were $140 million, up 0.9%.


Segment profit was $33 million, compared to $56 million in the year-ago quarter.


**Financial condition** On Sept. 30, cash and cash equivalents totaled $83.4 million, and total debt was $2.5 billion.


At Sept. 30, long-term debt included $1.7 billion of senior notes outstanding, $558 million of term loans outstanding and $274 million under the accounts receivable securitization facility. During the first nine months of 2026, we made principal pre-payments totaling $60.6 million on our June 2028 and November 2029 term loans.


Scripps did not declare or provide payment for any of the quarterly preferred stock dividends in 2026. The 9% dividend rate on the preferred shares compounds quarterly. At Sept. 30, aggregated undeclared and unpaid cumulative dividends totaled $166 million. Under the terms of Berkshire Hathaway’s preferred equity investment in Scripps, the company is prohibited from paying dividends on or repurchasing common shares until all preferred shares are redeemed.


***Year-to-date 2026 operating results:*** *The following comparisons are to the period ending Sept. 30, 2025:*


Revenue was $1.6 billion, a decrease of 2.4% or $38.2 million from the prior year. Political revenue was $122 million, compared to $11.9 million in the prior year, a non-election year.


Costs and expenses for segments, shared services and corporate were $1.3 billion, down from $1.4 billion in the year-ago period, reflecting tight expense controls and savings achieved through our enterprise-wide transformation plan.


Loss attributable to the shareholders of Scripps was $1.2 billion or $12.73 per share. The 2026 period included a non-cash goodwill and other intangible assets impairment charge for Scripps Networks of $1.1 billion, $55.3 million in restructuring costs and a $38.9 million gain from the sale of Court TV and two television stations: WFTX in Fort Myers, Florida, and WRTV in Indianapolis, as well as our stations swap with Gray Media, Inc. When taken together, these items increased the loss attributable to shareholders by $11.82 per share. In the prior year, loss attributable to the shareholders of Scripps was $120 million or $1.36 per share. The 2025 period included $44.5 million of financing transaction costs, a $31.4 million gain on our West Palm television station building sale, a $10.6 million loss on extinguishment of debt, $7.5 million in restructuring costs and a $7 million write-off of deferred financing costs. When taken together, these items increased the loss attributable to shareholders by 33 cents per share.


**Looking ahead** *Comparisons for our segments are to the same adjusted combined period in 2025.*

**About Scripps**[The E.W. Scripps Company](https://www.scripps.com/) (NASDAQ: SSP) is a diversified media company focused on creating connection. As one of the nation’s largest local TV broadcasters, Scripps serves communities with quality, objective local journalism and operates a portfolio of about 60 stations in 40 markets. Scripps reaches households across the U.S. with national news outlet Scripps News and popular entertainment brands ION, Bounce, Grit, ION Mystery, ION Plus and Laff. Scripps is the nation’s largest holder of broadcast spectrum. Scripps Sports serves professional and college sports leagues, conferences and teams with local market depth and national broadcast reach of up to 100% of TV households. Founded in 1878, Scripps is the steward of the Scripps National Spelling Bee, and its longtime motto is: “Give light and the people will find their own way.”
